title: Sebastian and the Rivergate
premise: Wren Winterbourne, a riverboat captain hiding from a past entangled with the fallen Republic of Vessany, pulls a sealed chest from the Rivergate shallows and finds documents proving the Republic's last minister survived—and where he hid the treasury that could reignite a war. The salvage fleet's ruthless commander, Odile Ferran, wants the chest and the wreck, and she knows Wren's real name. Racing the six tides before the wreck shifts into deep water, Wren must choose between burning the proof and staying invisible, or delivering it to the minister's exiled daughter and finally paying the debt of survival. In the end, Wren scuttles their own boat to block the salvage fleet, gives the documents to the daughter, and accepts arrest—only to be freed by the riverfolk whose loyalty they earned, choosing at last to live as someone with a name.
about_author: Ansel Montrose is a former barge hand who spent a decade working the inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction is known for tidal pacing, salt-stung prose, and characters who measure their lives in miles.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes Wren's careful, invisible life piloting the Marguerite, trading favors along the river and dodging questions about their past. When a spring flood recedes, it exposes a wreck in the Rivergate shallows—and a lead chest stamped with the Vessany seal. Emotional beat: the uneasy comfort of a life built on anonymity, cracked open by the river's gift.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren opens the chest alone: ship's manifests, a minister's sealed confession, and a map to the Vessany treasury. Their deckhand Tammi swears loyalty but notices Wren's hands shaking at the name signed inside. Emotional beat: dread—the past has a weight, and Wren has just picked it up.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. News travels faster than boats: the salvage fleet under Commander Odile Ferran is coming, and the wreck will sink past recovery in six tides. Wren realizes Ferran once hunted them for the Republic and will recognize their methods if not their face. Emotional beat: the clock starts; invisibility becomes a tactical problem.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts Wrecks
chapters.summary: Ferran's POV. Ferran interrogates riverfolk, burning a ferryman's license to loosen tongues. She reveals her own history: she served Vessany too, and she believes the treasury is her rightful pension. Emotional beat: the antagonist humanized—corruption shown as ambition wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Debt of a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren seeks out Ilse Vantor, the exiled minister's daughter, living poor in a river town, and finds she already suspects her father survived the Republic's fall. Wren lies about how they got the documents. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—Wren protects their secret at the cost of honesty with the one person who deserves it.

chapters.title: Third Tide, Rising
chapters.summary: Tammi's POV. Tammi discovers Wren's old Republic insignia hidden in the Marguerite's bilge and confronts them mid-voyage. Ferran's scouts shadow the boat. Tammi must decide whether the captain they trust is the traitor the fleet's posters describe. Emotional beat: betrayal's ambiguity—loyalty tested by a truth half-told.

chapters.title: The Wreck Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Diving the wreck at slack tide, Wren finds proof the minister died a coward who sold his own crew—and that Wren's own testimony, given under coercion years ago, sent him there. The confession implicates Wren as much as the dead. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; guilt surfaces with the wreck.

chapters.title: Ferran's Offer
chapters.summary: Ferran's POV. Ferran corners Wren at the Grackle tavern and offers a bargain: the documents for a clean name and a pardon, signed by the same magistrates who once condemned them. Wren almost takes it. Emotional beat: temptation—the corruption of power offered gently, and refused at real cost.

chapters.title: Scuttle the Marguerite
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with Tammi and Ilse. The climax: with one tide left, Wren deliberately sinks the Marguerite across the Rivergate channel, stranding the salvage fleet and destroying the wreck's location. Ferran takes Wren prisoner as the riverfolk watch. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the boat that was Wren's anonymity becomes their statement.

chapters.title: A Name on the Water
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, closing with Wren. Ilse publishes her father's confession and her own testimony; the riverfolk, led by Tammi, force Ferran's release of Wren and run her fleet off the water. Wren, nameless no longer, signs the manifest of a new boat. Emotional beat: resolution—the price of survival is paid, and living truthfully costs less than hiding ever did.
